images.caption: The 'Skew Bridge' at Norden. The remains of 'Skew Bridge' at Norden. The bridge formerly carried the narrow gauge Fayles Tramway over the standard gauge Wareham to Swanage line. The tramway carried clay mined locally to an interchange with the main line near the site of the current Norden Station. The standard gauge line is now the preserved Swanage Railway, whilst part of the tramway has been recreated on its original track bed within the adjacent Purbeck Mineral and Mining Museum. A reverse view to this one can be seen in this image, whilst a view of the bridge from abutment level can be seen in this image.

images.filename: Entrance to the Purbeck Mineral & Mining museum (geograph 5810294).jpg
images.caption: Entrance to the Purbeck Mineral & Mining museum. Situated at Norden station on the Swanage Railway. A small volunteer run museum that is dedicated to the history of Purbeck Ball Clay mining and the industrial heritage of Purbeck and the Purbeck narrow gauge railways. The clay industry was a major employer in Corfe Castle and the surrounding villages from the end of the 18th Century.
